elements.quote: Purpose This systematic literature review aimed to make a detailed overview on the clinical and functional outcomes and to get insight into the possible superiority of a treatment method for extra-articular distal radius fractures .
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly labels the work as a 'systematic literature review', identifying the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: Purpose This systematic literature review aimed to make a detailed overview on the clinical and functional outcomes and to get insight into the possible superiority of a treatment method for extra-articular distal radius fractures .
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective: to overview clinical and functional outcomes and assess possible superiority of treatment methods.
The abstract does not state the main inclusion or exclusion criteria (no eligibility criteria are reported in the abstract text).

elements.quote: Methods Embase, Medline, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for studies describing treatment results.
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources searched but does not report when each source was last searched (no search date provided in the abstract).
The abstract does not describe the methods used to assess risk of bias in included studies.
The abstract does not specify the methods used to present or synthesize results (e.g., meta-analysis model, summary measures); it reports findings but not synthesis methods.

elements.quote: Out of 7,054 screened studies, 109 were included in the analysis.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (109) but does not report the total number of participants in the abstract.

elements.quote: Overall complication rate ranged from 9% after plaster cast treatment to 18.5% after K-wire fixation. For radiographic outcomes, only volar tilt in the plaster cast group was lower than in the other groups. Apart from better grip strength after volar plating, no clear functional differences were found across treatment groups.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for main outcomes (complication rates, radiographic and functional findings) but does not provide numbers of included studies and participants for each specific outcome.

elements.quote: Overall complication rate ranged from 9% after plaster cast treatment to 18.5% after K-wire fixation.
elements.reason: The abstract reports summary estimates (complication rates) but does not provide confidence intervals or credible intervals for those summary estimates.

elements.quote: Apart from better grip strength after volar plating, no clear functional differences were found across treatment groups.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates a direction of effect (better grip strength) and which group is favored (volar plating) when comparing groups.
The abstract does not briefly summarize limitations of the included evidence (no mention of risk of bias, heterogeneity, imprecision, or other limitations in the abstract).

elements.quote: Conclusion Current literature does not provide uniform evidence to prove superiority of a particular treatment method when looking at complications, re-interventions, and long-term functional outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implication: that current literature does not support superiority of any particular treatment.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding.
The abstract does not provide any register name or registration number.

elements.quote: Current literature does not provide enough evidence to support superiority of a particular treatment method for extraarticular distal radius fractures, when looking at complications, re-interventions, and long-term functional outcomes. A broad range of outcome parameters have been used, which makes the data partly impossible to compare. From a methodological point of view, the quality of data used in this systematic review and subsequent conclusions that can be drawn, appear to be rather weak.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the current state of knowledge and important uncertainties (lack of evidence of superiority, heterogeneity of outcome measures, and weak methodological quality).

elements.quote: Purpose This systematic literature review aimed to make a detailed overview on the clinical and functional outcomes and to get insight into the possible superiority of a treatment method for extra-articular distal radius fractures .
elements.reason: The abstract states the purpose and explains the need to overview outcomes and investigate possible superiority of treatments, indicating the importance and rationale for conducting the review.
No text in the provided evidence discusses existing similar systematic reviews, nor cites or explains the need relative to prior reviews; therefore this reporting element is not reported.
The provided evidence does not describe a proposed mechanism of action for the interventions; only clinical outcomes and comparisons are reported without mechanistic explanation.

elements.quote: Five treatment modalities were compared: plaster cast immobilization, K-wire fixation, volar plating, external fixation, and intramedullary fixation .
elements.reason: The review compares discrete surgical and non-surgical treatment modalities rather than complex multi-component or delivery-context interventions; a logic model for complex interventions is therefore not applicable.

elements.quote: Purpose This systematic literature review aimed to make a detailed overview on the clinical and functional outcomes and to get insight into the possible superiority of a treatment method for extra-articular distal radius fractures .
elements.reason: The review objective is explicitly stated (to overview clinical and functional outcomes and assess possible superiority of treatments for extra-articular distal radius fractures), but it is not framed using a recognized question-formulation framework (e.g., PICO) in the provided text, so the requirement to use a relevant framework is only partially met.

elements.quote: Five treatment modalities were compared: plaster cast immobilization, K-wire fixation, volar plating, external fixation, and intramedullary fixation .
elements.reason: For an intervention review, the planned comparisons are stated by listing the five treatment modalities compared; the population (extra-articular distal radius fractures) and outcomes (clinical and functional outcomes, complications, re-interventions) are described elsewhere in the abstract and manuscript, fulfilling the PICO-style specification of planned comparisons.

elements.quote: The studies were eligible for inclusion if they met the following criteria: (1) Patients who suffered and were treated for an extra-articular distal radius fracture; (2) age 18 years or older; (3) patients were either treated using a plaster cast, K-wire(s), plate fixation, external fixator, or an intramedullary device; (4) primary data for at least one outcome parameter had to be available.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies key study characteristics used for eligibility: patient condition, age threshold, eligible interventions/treatments, and requirement for primary outcome data.

elements.quote: A literature search was conducted June 19, 2018. Embase, Medline, The Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched to identify relevant clinical studies that report on the outcomes of extra-articular distal radius fractures. ... No language limits were used and any potentially eligible non-English language manuscripts were translated if possible by native speaking colleagues or using Google translate, if no native speaker was available.
elements.reason: The review reports the search date and explicitly states no language limits (and translation approach), but it does not explicitly state restrictions by dissemination year beyond the search date or specify publication/report status criteria (e.g., grey literature inclusion/exclusion).

elements.quote: Studies without a clear description of fracture type or intervention, or studies that lacked sufficient data for analysis were excluded. In addition, studies with incomplete registration of complications were excluded.
elements.reason: The text lists exclusions for insufficient data or incomplete registration but does not distinguish exclusions because outcomes were not measured from exclusions because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: These 136 cohorts consisted of a total of 6707 patients divided over the five different treatment modalities. ... All outcome data were pooled for four different follow-up periods: 0-3 months, > 3-6 months, > 6-12 months, and 12 months or longer (long term).
elements.reason: The review specifies groups used in syntheses (five treatment modalities) and links outcome pooling to defined follow-up periods, aligning groups with comparisons of interest.

elements.quote: Studies describing a not-commonly used device or technique for extra-articular fractures were excluded ( i.e. dorsal plates, Epibloc system, cannulated screw, above elbow cast, etc.).
elements.reason: The manuscript provides a rationale for a notable restriction (exclusion of not-commonly used devices/techniques) and gives examples of such excluded interventions.

elements.quote: Meta-analysis for binary data was performed using MedCalc for Windows. ... Pooled estimates ( i.e., proportion) are reported with their 95% confidence intervals (CI). ... elements.quote: A random-effects model was used if the ­ I 2 value was larger than 40%. When the ­ I 2 was lower than 40% a fixed-effects model was used. ... When there was no overlap in the 95% confidence intervals, the difference was considered statistically significant.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports thresholds for choosing meta-analysis model (I2 > 40%) and a rule for interpreting statistical significance (no overlap of 95% CIs). It does not report thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect size magnitude (e.g., small/medium/large) or provide rationale for effect-size interpretation beyond these rules.
No description is provided of methods to re-express synthesized results using another effect measure.

elements.quote: Studies without a clear description of fracture type or intervention, or studies that lacked sufficient data for analysis were excluded. In addition, studies with incomplete registration of complications were excluded. Studies describing a not-commonly used device or technique for extra-articular fractures were excluded ( i.e. dorsal plates, Epibloc system, cannulated screw, above elbow cast, etc.). If a study consisted of one eligible and one non-eligible cohort, this study was included in our study, but only if data for the eligible group was provided. ... All outcome data were pooled for four different follow-up periods: 0-3 months, > 3-6 months, > 6-12 months, and 12 months or longer (long term).
elements.reason: The Methods/Data Analysis section explicitly states inclusion/exclusion rules used to determine study eligibility for synthesis (e.g., exclusions for unclear fracture type/intervention, insufficient data, incomplete complication registration, uncommon devices/techniques) and explains handling of mixed cohorts and the grouping of outcome data into defined follow-up periods for pooling.

elements.quote: Meta-analysis for binary data was performed using MedCalc for Windows. Heterogeneity testing was performed using Cochran's Q and the ­ I 2 statistic. Q is distributed as a chisquare statistic with k (number of studies) minus 1 degrees of freedom. Q has low power as a comprehensive test of heterogeneity [15]. The ­ I 2 statistic describes the percentage of variation across studies that is due to heterogeneity rather than chance [16, 17]. A random-effects model was used if the ­ I 2 value was larger than 40%. When the ­ I 2 was lower than 40% a fixed-effects model was used. Pooled estimates ( i.e., proportion) are reported with their 95% confidence intervals (CI). When there was no overlap in the 95% confidence intervals, the difference was considered statistically significant. For the continuous data a pooled estimate ( i.e., mean) was calculated in Microsoft Excel, using sample size as a weighting factor. Since most studies only provided the mean values but no standard deviation, 95% confidence interval, or standard error, a formal meta-analysis was not feasible for the continuous data.
elements.reason: The Methods/Data Analysis section explicitly describes how binary and continuous data were prepared and synthesized (software, heterogeneity testing, model selection rules, pooled estimates with 95% CIs, and how continuous data were pooled and limitations due to missing dispersion statistics).

elements.quote: The pooled average age and gender of patients for each treatment method are outlined in Table 1. ... The outcome data that were retrieved, consisted of; complications and re-interventions, radiographic outcomes ( i.e. consolidation rate, volar/dorsal tilt, radial inclination, radial height, and ulnar variance), range of motion, grip strength, and functional outcome scores ( i.e. Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH) score, Quick -DASH score, Patient Rated Wrist Evaluation (PRWE-)score, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain, Gartland and Werley score, and the Mayo Wrist Score). All outcome data were pooled for four different follow-up periods: 0-3 months, > 3-6 months, > 6-12 months, and 12 months or longer (long term).
elements.reason: Methods describe which data were extracted and indicate these data are shown in tables (e.g. Table 1) and how outcomes were pooled across defined follow-up periods, supporting description of tabular content.

elements.reason: The authors state which model (random- versus fixed-effects) was used and provide a rationale based on the I2 threshold ( >40%).

Diaz-Garcia et al. published a systematic review in 2011 to examine outcomes of unstable distal radius fractures after treatment with either volar locking plate, non-bridging external fixation, bridging external fixation, percutaneous Kirschner-wire fixation, or plaster cast immobilization. elements.quote: This systematic review had several limitations. First, most studies that were included were retrospective or prospective observational studies, with disappointing reporting quality for continuous data. For a proper meta-analysis of continuous data the mean, a measure of dispersion (either standard deviation, standard error or confidence interval), and sample size are necessary. Many studies in this review failed to provide these data. Moreover, the number of large, well-designed RCTs on extra-articular fractures is very low, and therefore it is very well possible to have a type 2 error. Second, selection bias in the source studies might have influenced the results of the meta-analysis, since stable and simple extra-articular fractures might have been treated nonoperatively, whereas the more dislocated and comminuted fractures might have been treated by volar plating or external fixator. However, current data did not allow for metaregression analyses. Therefore, it is not entirely certain if the current whether the findings are related to the treatment type, or can be explained by a difference in indication. Third, there was high heterogeneity in type of outcome parameters and time points of measurements reported. Goldhahn et al. mentioned already in 2014 that this heterogeneity is problematic in research on distal radius fractures and suggested a set of core domains to assess outcomes as a possible solution [129]. We have not discovered any clear improvement in data consistency since this article has been published.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly lists multiple limitations of the included evidence: study designs (mostly observational), poor reporting of continuous data preventing meta-analysis, few large RCTs (risk of type II error), selection bias in source studies, inability to perform metaregression, and high heterogeneity of outcomes and time points.
